newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar asks court TO postpone November poll.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar asks court TO postpone November poll.

text.p: Madagascar's interim President Norbert Ratsirahonana asked the High Court on Wednesday to delay presidential elections slated for November 3, a government spokesman said.
Ratsirahonana told the court technical and financial problems made it difficult to hold elections on that date but vowed his government would respect any High Court decision.

"In the light of financial problems and the many technical and material difficulties, the interim government fears that it may not be ready by the November date already decided by the High Court," the spokesman said.
The government would however "maintain a position of strict neutrality" and non interference in the High Court's decision, he said.
The election date has become the focus of a political battle between impeached President Albert Zafy and the interim government.
Zafy has threatened there may be trouble in Madagascar if the November 3 date set after he was thrown out is not respected.

Zafy, who became president in 1993, says he will run in the election despite being impeached by parliament on September 4 for alleged violations of the constitution and actions against the people's interests.
The impeachment capped three years of political instability on the Indian Ocean island which has a population of 14 million.
